summary: Steel fire tower built about 1935 near Salamander Rock in Frederick's watershed; removed, with concrete footings and stone ruins left.

facts.design: 100-foot all-steel tower with an interior metal staircase to a small cab

staffing.status: city-staffed on weekends during the war years; no later staffing is recorded in the sources

facts.status_note: Steel tower removed; four concrete footings and a roofless stone building remain.

visit.trail_note: A hiking trail known as Salamander Trail runs nearby; there is no tower to climb.

events.note: Built about 1935 (MHT: ca. 1935); March 1935 paper reported state approval of a 100-foot all-steel tower
City of Frederick transferred about one acre to the State of Maryland for a forest fire lookout
Forest supervisor said in August 1949 the tower had been open for some time as a precautionary move; no staffing schedule is given
Tower slated for removal in 1970; the sources do not give the date it came down

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1935 newspaper quote places the tower on city watershed property south of Salamander Rock; the later MHT form places the site near the summit. Treated as the same general site on the rock.

sources.title: Determination of Eligibility Form, Salamander Fire Tower (F-3-286)
Column: Fire detection towers served the watershed

notes_for_editor: The 1935 and 1949 newspaper items are known only through quotations on the Forest Lookouts page; the original papers were not read. The Frederick News-Post column is partly obscured in the cached copy, so only its plain paragraphs are quoted. The MHT form's header box reads 'NR Eligible: yes' while its prose says not eligible under Criterion A; the prose is used. The record's 30.5 m height matches the 100-foot figure. The 1949 item is typed 'other' because the source says only that the tower had been open for some time. No photos found; the Frederick News-Post captions carry a 'Courtesy photo' credit with no source link. Access is not stated in any source, so no access key is given. Weebly's 'south of Salamander Rock' versus MHT's 'near the summit' is noted as a resolved conflict.
